# Why a multinomial model?

The binary outcome used earlier distinguishes low/no-to-mild post-treatment severity from moderate-or-worse severity. Sometimes the question concerns how treatment redistributes probability across **three or more unordered outcome categories**.

We use these teaching categories:

- `low_no_to_mild`: LSAS < 50;
- `moderate_marked`: 50 ≤ LSAS < 80; and
- `severe_very_severe`: LSAS ≥ 80.

They are a pedagogical severity grouping, not validated diagnostic or remission thresholds.

# Long data for `mlogit`

`mlogit` represents a multinomial outcome as a choice among alternatives. Each participant therefore appears once for every possible severity category. One and only one alternative is marked as the observed outcome.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(mlogit)
library(marginaleffects)

df_outcome <- read_csv2(here("data", "steps_clean.csv")) |>
  filter(!is.na(lsas_post), !is.na(trt)) |>
  mutate(
    severity_observed = case_when(
      lsas_post < 50 ~ "low_no_to_mild",
      lsas_post < 80 ~ "moderate_marked",
      TRUE ~ "severe_very_severe"
    ),
    severity_observed = factor(
      severity_observed,
      levels = c("low_no_to_mild", "moderate_marked", "severe_very_severe")
    ),
    trt = factor(trt,
      levels = c("waitlist", "therapist-guided", "self-guided")
    )
  ) |>
  select(id, trt, severity_observed)

long <- crossing(
  df_outcome,
  severity_alt = levels(df_outcome$severity_observed)
) |>
  mutate(choice = severity_alt == severity_observed)

long |>
  count(id) |>
  count(n)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 1 × 2
      n    nn
  <int> <int>
1     3   169
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mlogit_data <- mlogit.data(
  long,
  choice = "choice",
  shape = "long",
  chid.var = "id",
  alt.var = "severity_alt",
  drop.index = TRUE
)
```
:::


# Fit a treatment model


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mod_multinomial <- mlogit(
  choice ~ 1 | trt,
  data = mlogit_data,
  reflevel = "low_no_to_mild"
)
summary(mod_multinomial)
```

The coefficient table uses log-odds contrasts against the reference severity category. We will instead focus on model-based probabilities for each outcome category.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Supply the ordinary long data frame, rather than mlogit_data, to
# marginaleffects when requesting predictions.
severity_probabilities <- avg_predictions(
  mod_multinomial,
  newdata = as.data.frame(long),
  by = "trt"
)
severity_probabilities
```

## Probability redistribution

The following custom hypothesis calculates therapist-guided minus waitlist probability differences separately for each severity category.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
therapist_minus_waitlist <- function(x) {
  x |>
    group_by(.data$group, .data$trt) |>
    summarize(estimate = mean(.data$estimate), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = "trt", values_from = "estimate") |>
    transmute(
      term = .data$group,
      estimate = .data[["therapist-guided"]] - .data$waitlist
    )
}

severity_differences <- predictions(
  mod_multinomial,
  newdata = as.data.frame(long),
  hypothesis = therapist_minus_waitlist
)
severity_differences
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Model interpretation

Compared with waitlist, therapist-guided treatment changes the estimated probability of low/no-to-mild severity by **30.4 percentage points** (95% CI **15.1** to **45.7 percentage points**).

The probability of severe/very severe symptoms changes by **-28.3 percentage points** (95% CI **-44.2** to **-12.4 percentage points**). The category probabilities must sum to one, so an increase in one category is accompanied by decreases elsewhere.
:::


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
severity_probabilities |>
  ggplot(aes(x = trt, y = estimate, color = group, group = group)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = .2)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
    width = .1,
    position = position_dodge(width = .2)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated post-treatment severity probabilities",
    subtitle = "Multinomial logit; 95% confidence intervals",
    x = "Treatment group",
    y = "Estimated probability",
    color = "Severity category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Summary

- Multinomial logit models probabilities for multiple outcome categories.
- `mlogit` needs a long participant-by-alternative data structure.
- Interpret the model as a redistribution of outcome probabilities, not as isolated coefficient changes.
- The probability differences for the categories sum to zero across any treatment contrast.
